{"id":"vouch-xlha.18","title":"migrate: git replace refs swap keys/ content under C's valid signature","description":"git-vouch-migrate:340-346 (Pgpkeys.__init__: rev-parse, show, archive via plain 'git') and 454-462 (check_signature: git verify-commit).

git-vouch runs git as GIT = ['git', '--no-replace-objects'] (git-vouch:213); migrate uses plain 'git', so refs/replace/* in the pgpkeys clone apply. C's commit object (and so its signature) is untouched, but git archive reads replaced trees/blobs under keys/. Result: 'pgpkeys at C, signed by <signer>' is printed while the keyring holds keys that are not in C. This breaks DESIGN.md:662 / flag-day.md:82 'reads pgpkeys only at C'.

Trigger: a clone with replace refs, e.g. 'git clone --mirror' (refspec +refs/*:refs/*) of an untrusted pgpkeys mirror, or 'git fetch origin refs/*:refs/*'. Also GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE in the environment.

Reproduced (gpg 2.4.4, git 2.55): signed C with keys/alice.asc; 'git replace <alice blob> <mallory key blob>'; port C --signer <maint> -> signature check passes and people/mallory.json is drafted with Mallory's fingerprint; Alice is absent. The same substitution feeds verify-continuity and drafts.

Fix: run every git command in Pgpkeys with vouch.GIT (or set GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 in the env for verify-commit too).
